rows.24:9b30: Went into the restroom in the new school building
rows.24:9b48: Went to the old school building restroom from before
rows.24:9b80:
Holding it in isn't good for your body, after all.
I decided to go to the restroom on the first floor of the new school building.
But at that moment, I'd forgotten.
I'd forgotten that Takeuchi's classroom was on the first floor...
I wanted to get home quickly, so I walked briskly toward the restroom.{p}
rows.24:9c64:
I went into the new school building and hurried down the first-floor hallway, almost at a run.
And then...{p}
rows.24:9cc0:
I heard footsteps behind me.
At first I was rushing along in such a panic that I didn't notice the sound.
The footsteps came closer, and a chill ran through me.
Someone was following me.
That's what I thought.
The restroom was only a little farther.
Should I make a run for it and hide in one of the stalls?
That crossed my mind too.
The footsteps kept coming closer and closer.
...I had no choice but to run!
I was just about to break into a run.
And then...!{p}
rows.24:9e44:
"Hosoda. You saw what happened back there, didn't you?"
A voice came from behind me.{p}
rows.24:9ea8:
It was Takeuchi.
"Now that you've seen that, I can't let you live.
Let's see... Maybe I'll drop you into that toilet.
I'll make you food for that thing."
It was a terrifying voice.
I couldn't believe it belonged to Takeuchi, the guy everyone adored...
"I saw you running away from there.
I was planning to deal with you tomorrow or so... but fancy you coming right up to my classroom.
How convenient.
I'll get rid of you right now."
He lunged at me and grabbed hold of me.{p}
rows.24:a048:
I fought back with everything I had.
Somebody must have seen what was going on.
After a while, a teacher came running.
I was saved.
Takeuchi clicked his tongue and went home.
...After that, he ended up transferring to another school.{p}
rows.24:a12c:
It must have been because of what happened.
I never told anyone about it, though.
I had a feeling he'd kill me if I did.
On his last day, you should have seen how sad everyone was.{p}
rows.24:a1e4:
After all, he'd been in the girls' spotlight as the guy who never went to the restroom.
He went around saying his goodbyes, carrying paper bags stuffed with presents and letters from girls.{p}
rows.24:a284:
And at the very end, he walked off toward the old school building.
Someone said they saw him.
Had he gone to say goodbye to that plant, too?
I couldn't stop wondering what had become of that restroom.
So the next day, I went to take a look.
And then...
He was there.{p}
rows.24:a3b8:
The plant growing out of the toilet had two of Takeuchi's faces on it.
One of the faces said this:
"Help me..."
Takeuchi had tried to get rid of that plant.
But the plant struck back, dragged him into the toilet, and made him its food, it seems.
That's what Takeuchi's face on the plant told me, weeping.
Apparently, when Takeuchi first came to this school, he explored the old school building.
That's how he found that plant.
The plant grew by feeding on his waste...
My hunch had been right.
Takeuchi only ever used the old school building's restroom, so nobody ever saw him going to the restroom.
But...{p}
rows.24:a630:
Takeuchi had been tricked.
The plant had told him, apparently, that by absorbing his waste it would take on his exact shape, until in the end it couldn't be told apart from a human.
Takeuchi wanted to make a clone of himself.
I guess he wanted to do sci-fi stuff, like the two of them taking turns going to class or going out to have fun.
That's why he'd been dutifully making trips there.
But the idea that it could make a clone was a lie.
The plant's real goal was to make a human into its food...
I just ran from that place.
There was no way I had the power to save Takeuchi.
And I swore I'd never go there again.
Even after I got out of the restroom and was running down the hallway, I could hear Takeuchi screaming.
He cried out again and again, in agony.
I can still hear it now.
Takeuchi's screams.
His voice calling for help...
...
I've told you everything I saw.
Now, shall we move on to the next story...{p}
rows.24:a998:
Maybe I really should have used the new school building's restroom.
But I just couldn't stop thinking about what I'd seen back there.
So I decided to go to the old school building one more time.
Can you believe I tried to use a restroom with that plant in it?
Now that I think about it, maybe the plant was calling me.
I headed for the old school building.{p}
rows.24:aaf4:
When I went into the old school building, I heard someone crying.
I had a really bad feeling.
Maybe I shouldn't have come to a place like this after all.
That's what I thought, but my feet kept carrying me toward the restroom.
The closer I got to the restroom, the louder the crying became.
And then, as if something were drawing me in, I opened the door to that restroom.{p}
rows.24:acc4:
When I looked inside, the plant...
The plant with Takeuchi's face was crying.
The Takeuchi in human form wasn't there anymore.
And the plant was saying something like this:
"Help me...!
I'm Takeuchi.
An evil spirit turned me into this.
Help me... please... help me..."
He told me the whole story.
On the first day Takeuchi came to this school, he snuck into the old school building as a prank.
While he was there, he needed to use the restroom...
When he used that toilet, an evil spirit's hand came out of the bowl and grabbed his leg, it seems.
The evil spirit sucked the life energy out of Takeuchi's body.
And Takeuchi was turned into a plant, he said.
After that, the evil spirit took on Takeuchi's exact form...
And started coming to school in his place, he told me.
Every so often, the evil spirit would come to Takeuchi and suck out his life energy.
It drained the energy out of Takeuchi, that shriveled-up plant, like it was wringing him dry.
I guess evil spirits don't go to the bathroom.
That's why Takeuchi got the reputation of never going to the restroom.
Nobody must have known he'd been making trips to the old school building's restroom.
Takeuchi, now a plant, was wailing.
But there was nothing I could do.
I apologized to him over and over, and left the old school building's restroom behind...{p}
rows.24:b194:
{a}{f:|}.
The evil spirit that disguised itself as Takeuchi has already graduated, but...
Maybe, even now, Takeuchi the plant is still in the old school building's restroom.
What do you say?
I'd like to go take a look right now...{p}
rows.24:b32c:
The air in the old school building was terribly damp.
The creaking hallway floor put everyone more and more on edge.{p}
rows.24:b398:
{f:We|We} came to the front of that restroom.
And when we opened the stall door Hosoda pointed at...{p}
rows.24:b41c:
"...There's nothing here."
There was no plant {f:at all|or anything} in the toilet.
Everyone looked relieved.
But Hosoda alone looked troubled.
He looked like he wanted to say something.
"Hosoda, what's wrong?"
{f:I|I} worked up the nerve to ask.{p}
rows.24:b550:
"{a}{f:|}, this is really hard to say, but..."
Hosoda began to mumble.
...Do you know why I brought you here?
Because there was one thing bothering me.
And that hunch turned out to be right.
Takeuchi, the one who became a plant, must be dead by now.
And if so...
That means the evil spirit Takeuchi has no one left to give it life energy.
Someone else might get turned into a plant here.
...{a}{f:|}.
I'll tell you what I'm worried about.
You look like Takeuchi.
How do I put it... it's your aura... your eyes, things like that.
{f:Being told this out of the blue|Being told you look like a guy} {f:probably puts you on the spot|might not mean much to you}, though.
The evil spirit disguised as Takeuchi might have already turned someone else into a plant.
Maybe its prey doesn't even have to look like Takeuchi.
But I'm worried.
That you, with that same air as Takeuchi...
Might become the next victim...
...
Now, let's go back to the club room.
We have to hear the next story, after all...{p}
rows.24:b9d0:
Later, I thought maybe I should have gone after all.
Takeuchi had invited me, of all people.{p}
rows.24:baf0:
It couldn't be helped, so after school that day I went to see him again.
Just then, Takeuchi happened to come out of the classroom.
He ran off down the hallway.
Without thinking, I went after him.{p}
rows.24:bbc0:
Then Takeuchi headed for the old school building.
Why would he go to the old school building, of all places?
His suspicious behavior bothered me, so I kept following him.
And he went straight to the restroom.{p}
rows.24:bc88:
"I have something to do today.
Could we make it another day?"
"I see. Then when's good for you?"
Takeuchi asked kindly.
We settled on a day for me to visit his house.
And then that day came.{p}
rows.24:bdf8:
After a while, the coffee was brought in.
...Or so I thought, but I got a shock.
It had a strange smell.
That drink wasn't coffee.
It looked exactly like coffee, though.
And Takeuchi smiled and said this:
"I'll let you taste something rarer than coffee.
Take a look.
This is called Sanbura tea.
It's from abroad.
A souvenir from my father's travels.
Once you drink it, it's pretty addictive."
A grassy smell, like bitter medicinal herbs, drifted from the cart carrying the Sanbura tea.
That choking smell...
I felt like I was going to be sick.
So what do you think I did with the tea he offered me?{p}
rows.24:c044:
"Oh, anything.
Whatever... juice or... no, anything's fine."
I was really nervous.
So I didn't even know what I was saying myself.
Then Takeuchi came out with this:
"Then how about tea?
I've got a good one right now.
It's called Sanbura tea."
Sanbura tea?
"It's a souvenir my dad brought back from a trip abroad.
Apparently it's not something you can find on the open market.
Once you drink it, it's pretty addictive."
Saying that, Takeuchi poured me some Sanbura tea.{p}
rows.24:c258:
It was a murky, pitch-black color.
It had a grassy smell, like bitter medicinal herbs.
"It has an unusual taste, so people might either love it or hate it, but once you get used to it, it's irresistible.
Go on, try it."
...What would you do in a moment like this?{p}
rows.24:c348:
"Then, tea, please..."
When I asked for it, he gave me a big smile.
"Hosoda, I have an interesting drink.
It's something my dad got when he went abroad.
It's called Sanbura tea, and once you drink it, it's pretty addictive."{p}
rows.24:c4a0:
It tasted sour, like a pickled plum dropped into flush-toilet water.
And like someone had stuffed bugs into it...
It was a grassy, foul-tasting tea.
...Well, that's just how it seemed to me.
I've never actually drunk toilet water.
But it really was awful.
Still, I couldn't exactly spit it out.
I gulped down the tea in my mouth in one go.{p}
rows.24:c614:
Then Takeuchi broke into a huge grin and said this:
"You drank it.
Then I'll tell you my secret..."
My heart was pounding.
What was he going to say, I wondered...
"You've heard the rumor about me, right?
...The one about me never going to the restroom."
Takeuchi came closer to me.
"It's true."
I swallowed hard.
"The secret is in this... Sanbura tea."
Takeuchi put his hand on my shoulder.
"If you drink Sanbura tea, you won't need to go to the restroom anymore.
And your body's whole constitution changes amazingly."
Takeuchi peered into my face.
His lukewarm breath brushed my cheek...
And that breath smelled very grassy.{p}
rows.24:c8a8:
But for some reason, that grassy smell felt incredibly good.
So I leaned forward to breathe it in.
And then...
I saw it.{p}
rows.24:c958:
Under the skin of Takeuchi's cheek, little green things were wriggling around.
They looked like the microorganisms you see when you peer through a microscope.
Takeuchi may have caught the look on my face.
"There's no need to be afraid.
These are a kind of plant.
They become active once they get inside a human body.
Just like animals.
And they eat up all the impurities for you.
So there's no need to be afraid.
There's nothing scary about it at all."
That's what he started saying.{p}
rows.24:cb44:
And as he said it, the inside of his mouth was completely covered with what looked like earth-colored plant vines, or roots.
I'd already drunk the Sanbura tea.
At the time, I thought I'd end up like that too, and I was terrified, but...
...{p}
rows.24:cc40:
{a}{f:|}.
Sanbura tea is the best.
I've actually drunk it myself, so you can take my word for it.
Here, a present for you.
I brought it here just for you.{p}
rows.24:cce8:
Hosoda took out a drink container and set it on the desk.
No way, is this...!
A grassy smell stung my nose.
{f:I|I} fearfully took the container from him.
"So this is... Sanbura tea."
When {f:I|I} opened the lid of the container...{p}
rows.24:ce7c:
"Oh, sorry, sorry.
{a}{f:|}, I forgot to squeeze this into juice."
Hosoda gave a mysterious smile and slowly began to explain.
"...This is what Sanbura tea is made from.
A plant that feeds on impurities lives as a parasite in this bug's guts.
If you boil down the bug's body fluids, you can extract that plant's breeding essence.
That's what Sanbura tea is.
Of course, this plant eats human impurities too.
It eats the impurities, breaks them down, and turns what would normally become waste into sweat.
I'd heard this tea becomes addictive once you get used to it, and it's true.{p}
rows.24:d09c:
These days, I always buy these bugs from Takeuchi..."
Hosoda put his hand on {f:my|my} shoulder.
His breath smelled grassy.
And the thing squirming in his mouth...!
Hosoda seemed to notice {f:my|my} gaze.
He hurriedly covered his mouth with his hand.{p}
rows.24:d1b8:
"{a}{f:|}, I'm sorry.
I couldn't let you taste the Sanbura tea.
Next time, I'll make it properly and bring it in.
Then you won't have to go to the restroom either..."
Every time Hosoda spoke, the grassy smell stung {f:my|my} nose.
{f:No way|No way}.
There's no way {f:I could|I'd ever} drink something that creepy.
Time to have him wrap up his story, so we could hurry on to the next one...{p}
rows.24:d340:
Something pricked me at my feet.
What was that...?{p}
rows.24:d4c4:
Seeing that, Hosoda grinned.
"You just got bitten by the bug, didn't you?"
He said it, his shoulders shaking with delight.
What should I do?
If being bitten causes a change in {f:my|my} body...
"My story ends here..."
Hosoda picked up the Sanbura tea bug and murmured, truly delighted.
"{a}{f:|}, whose story are you going to hear next?"
{f:Oh no|Oh no}.
For a while, {f:I|I} couldn't say anything.
...
But...
{f:I|I} {f:didn't drink|never drank} the Sanbura tea.
Nothing strange {f:should happen.|is going to happen, right?}
It's fine.
I'm sure it's {f:fine|fine}...
{f:I|I} decided to hear the next person's story, though a lump of unease stayed in my chest.
"Well then, the next story..."{p}
rows.24:d804:
It was like mashed-up maggots mixed with cake and white bean paste, then thinned with muddy water.
...Maybe that's a bit of an exaggeration.
But anyway, it was disgusting.
And it clung thickly to the inside of my mouth.
Takeuchi smiled and said:{p}
rows.24:d8f8:
"Hosoda, that's my secret.
If you drink Sanbura tea, you instantly stop needing to go to the restroom.
And your body's whole constitution changes amazingly."
With that, Takeuchi slowly crept closer.
Close enough that his breath brushed my cheek.
...That breath smelled very grassy.{p}
rows.24:da10:
I went to Takeuchi's classroom.
Takeuchi was inside.
I could tell right away.
I mean, there were tons of girls crowded around.
But even though I'd made it to the classroom door, I couldn't go in, or even ask someone to call Takeuchi out.
I mean, it was a third-year classroom, and I didn't really know Takeuchi that well.
I'd come all this way, but I didn't know what to do.
Then...
To my surprise, Takeuchi spoke to me first.{p}
rows.24:dbd8:
"Hey, Hosoda.
Thanks for the other day."
"Oh, uh, h-h-hi.
Hello."
I stuttered so badly it was embarrassing.
"Hm? What's up?
Did you need something from me?"
Takeuchi was all smiles, chatting with me in a friendly way, like a completely different person from the other day.
"Oh, no, it's not that I needed anything in particular..."
"Perfect timing, Hosoda.
If you're free at lunch break today, could you come to the same place as before?
I think we'd get along, and I'd like to talk with you."
It was a chance I couldn't have hoped for.
I'd gone all the way there because I wanted to talk to Takeuchi.
I promised I'd definitely come, and left.{p}
rows.24:de24:
Then came lunch break.
I wolfed down my lunch and went behind the old school building.{p}
rows.24:de7c:
Takeuchi was already there.
"Oh, sorry I'm late."
"No, it's fine.
I just got here myself."
Takeuchi said it with a smile.
"More importantly, do you have a minute?"
"Yes, what is it?"
"I want to go to the restroom for a bit. Will you come with me?"
I was stunned.
I mean, Takeuchi was famous for never going to the restroom, and here he was saying that.
Seeing me gaping in astonishment, Takeuchi laughed and said this:
"Aren't you getting the wrong idea?
I said I'm going to the restroom, but it's not to relieve myself.
There's something I want to go get."{p}
rows.24:e0e4:
I was a little relieved.
Why, you ask?
In my mind, Takeuchi was a superman who never went to the restroom, or a hero, or something...
Anyway, I'd finally gotten close to someone like that, so finding out he was just an ordinary person would have been a letdown.
I think I didn't want my image of an 'amazing person' right near me to be shattered.
So I followed Takeuchi into the old school building.{p}
rows.24:e310:
It was a flower growing in a flowerpot, some kind I'd never seen before.
"What is this?"
I asked him straight out.
"Heh heh.
This is my secret for never going to the restroom."
Takeuchi said it just like that.
I was a little surprised.
I wondered why he'd tell me his secret so easily.
I'd just assumed it had to be some incredible secret, like a secret technique passed down in his family and never revealed to outsiders.
"You mustn't tell anyone.
I'm only telling you because it's you, Hosoda."
When he said that, I was so happy.
I promised I'd never tell anyone.{p}
rows.24:e574:
Then Takeuchi carefully hugged the flowerpot and went back out to the yard behind the old school building.
"Hosoda, watch this."
With that, Takeuchi set the flowerpot down in a sunny spot.
(Huh?)
The flower in the pot started writhing and moving!
At first I thought the parts that had shriveled up were just spreading out in the sun.
But I was wrong.{p}
rows.24:e6c8:
When the sun hit it, the flower started moving as if it had a will of its own.
The petals snapped wide open, and inside were rows of what looked like tiny teeth.
And it began moving, looking this way and that, as if searching for prey.
Takeuchi gently stroked the petals, rolled up his shirt sleeve, and thrust his arm out in front of the flower.
The instant he did, the plant bit into Takeuchi's arm!
"T-Takeuchi☆"
I couldn't help screaming.{p}
rows.24:e888:
"It's okay, Hosoda...
This is how I have the flower suck out the things my body doesn't need.
That way, I don't have to go to the restroom."
Takeuchi said it with a look of ecstasy.
Blood oozed from where the flower had bitten him and dripped down.
"There, I'm done.
Next, it's your turn, Hosoda."{p}
rows.24:e9c0:
With that, Takeuchi thrust the flowerpot at me.
I didn't know what to do.
I mean, just watching it, it looked really painful.
Besides, I didn't want to be bitten by something I didn't understand.
I refused with everything I had.
Then Takeuchi, disappointed, said to me:{p}
rows.24:eadc:
"Hosoda.
I'm so disappointed.
I went to the trouble of telling you a secret I've never told anyone.
Once you don't have to go to the restroom, all sorts of good things happen.
First, you don't have to go to the restroom.
That way, you don't have to spend the precious time of your life on the restroom.
Time you've lost never comes back, after all.
Next, you get really popular with girls.
Even if they're not actually into you, they flock around to ask how to stop needing the restroom.
It feels great.
Being surrounded by girls.
But those two things aren't really a big deal.
There's something even better.
Want to know?
I'll tell you.
When the flower is sucking from you, it feels really good.
It's like having the toxins drawn out of your body...
It's a pleasure only people who've experienced it can understand.
You had the chance to taste it, and you're just going to let it slip away? I can't imagine that.
You might never get another chance to taste it."
Takeuchi said it like he was truly disappointed.
Hearing that, I started to feel like I was throwing a once-in-a-lifetime chance down the drain.{p}
rows.24:ef00:
(How good could it feel?
If Takeuchi recommends it that strongly, it must be amazing.
If I let this chance slip by now, I'll probably never get to taste it again...)
Thinking that, I couldn't shake the feeling that if I didn't try it now, I'd regret it for the rest of my life.
So I decided to let him do it.{p}
rows.24:f048:
"Takeuchi.
I've changed my mind, and I want to give it a try.
Please.
Let me give it a try."
I asked him with a serious face.
Then Takeuchi said,
"Oh, Hosoda.
You're up for it now?
You're just what I took you for.
You know, I was thinking it wasn't right for me to keep this all to myself.
I thought you'd surely understand how I feel, Hosoda.
My eye for people didn't fail me."{p}
rows.24:f1dc:
With that, he thrust the flowerpot toward me, looking really, really happy.
On the flowerpot, that flower was writhing and squirming, hungry for prey.
I was scared, but I wanted to taste the pleasure Takeuchi talked about.
I took the plunge and held out my right arm.{p}
rows.24:f2fc:
The flower reared up as if it were roaring, then bit into my arm.
"Ow!"
Without thinking, I swung my right arm around, the one it was biting, trying to shake it off.
But the flower kept its teeth firmly in my right arm and wouldn't let go.
And it was sucking my blood.{p}
rows.24:f42c:
It hurt the instant it bit me, but having my blood sucked felt really good.
How can I put it... it really was like having the dirt sucked out of my body; I felt refreshed, and it felt like my body was getting lighter and lighter.
The heaviness I'd always felt in my body vanished like it had never been there.
Feeling completely fulfilled, I spoke to Takeuchi.{p}

notes: 24:a3b8: 'two of Takeuchi's faces' kept literal; source gives no explanation for the second face.
24:a630/24:a12c: in this branch Takeuchi transfers; in the 24:acc4 branch the spirit 'graduated' (24:b194). Kept as written, branches differ.
